io.reader

Class EventExcelReader

  • java.lang.Object
    • io.reader.EventExcelReader
  • All Implemented Interfaces:
    ExcelReadable, Readable, java.lang.AutoCloseable, java.lang.Iterable<java.lang.String[]>

    public class EventExcelReader
extends java.lang.Object
implements ExcelReadable, java.lang.Iterable<java.lang.String[]>
    Reads Excel XLSX workbooks using Apache POI’s event-based API to reduce memory consumption when processing large worksheets.

    Implements ExcelReadable to provide tabular access to worksheet data without constructing a complete in-memory worksheet model, such as a memory-intensive DOM model and other alternatives.

    Worksheet XML is parsed using a SAX parser, allowing cell data to be processed incrementally rather than loading the entire worksheet into a DOM tree. This approach can reduce memory consumption, although actual usage depends on the workbook contents and the data retained by the reader.

    Shared strings are accessed through Apache POI’s ReadOnlySharedStringsTable, which provides read-only access to shared-string data without requiring the standard mutable shared strings table.

    Cell values are exposed as strings. Loading the workbook’s style table is optional and enables style-dependent interpretation of values, such as dates and specially formatted numbers. The style table can be excluded when this interpretation is not required.

    Change history:

    • 10 December 2017 — Initial implementation by Trevor Maggs.
    • 9 October 2026 — Reorganised under io.reader, introduced TabularDataException, reviewed stream handling, and standardised method ordering.

    10 December 2017

      • findColumnIndexByContent

        public int findColumnIndexByContent(java.lang.String entry,
                                    int rowIndex)
        Finds the first column in the specified row whose cell value equals the specified text, ignoring case and leading or trailing whitespace.

        A null search value is treated as an empty string. Null cell values are skipped, while empty-string cell values can match an empty search value.

        Specified by:
        findColumnIndexByContent in interface Readable
        Parameters:
        entry - text to match or null is treated as an empty string
        rowIndex - zero-based index of the row to search
        Returns:
        zero-based column index of the first matching cell, or -1 if no match is found or the row index is invalid

      • findColumnIndexRegex

        public int findColumnIndexRegex(java.lang.String regex,
                                int rowIndex)
        Finds the first column in the specified row whose cell value matches the specified regular expression, ignoring case.

        The cell value is trimmed before matching, and the expression must match the entire value. If the expression is invalid, it is treated as literal text as a fallback value.

        Specified by:
        findColumnIndexRegex in interface Readable
        Parameters:
        regex - regular expression to match, or literal text if the expression is invalid
        rowIndex - zero-based index of the row to search
        Returns:
        zero-based column index of the first matching cell, or -1 if no match is found, regex is null, or rowIndex is invalid

      • iterator

        public java.util.Iterator<java.lang.String[]> iterator()
        Returns an iterator over the rows of the active worksheet.

      • getSheetCount

        public int getSheetCount()
        Returns the number of worksheets in the workbook.

        It may return 0 if the worksheet list cannot be obtained. Therefore, a return value of 0 does not necessarily mean the workbook contains no worksheets.

        Specified by:
        getSheetCount in interface ExcelReadable
        Returns:

      • fetchWorksheetList

        public static java.util.List<java.lang.String> fetchWorksheetList(java.nio.file.Path fpath)
                                                           throws TabularDataException
        Fetches a list of current available worksheet names defined in the workbook.

        It uses a StAX event reader to inspect the workbook metadata without building a DOM tree of the XML document. Worksheet names are returned in workbook order.

        Parameters:
        fpath - to the XLSX workbook
        Returns:
        worksheet names in workbook order
        Throws:
        TabularDataException - if the workbook cannot be opened or its worksheet metadata cannot be read
